quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Where should your feet be when riding?

options.text: On the gas tank.
Hanging down.
On the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests while riding. This helps you stay balanced.

questions.question: When should you use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch?

options.text: When the throttle gets stuck and you cannot free it.
When you start to lose control in a curve.
When the motorcycle starts to wobble.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the throttle gets stuck and you cannot free it.
questions.explanation: If the throttle gets stuck and you cannot free it, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch right away. This stops power to the rear wheel so you can safely stop.

questions.question: When riding in the left third of the lane so a car driver can see you in their side mirror, what is the problem?

options.text: Most drivers do not check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
Wind may block the use of a side mirror.
Drivers should not use side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers do not check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane. This puts you in the driver's rearview mirror where they are more likely to see you.

questions.question: What should a working clutch feel like before you ride?

options.text: Loose and rough.
Tight and smooth.
Loose and smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tight and smooth.
questions.explanation: Check your clutch and throttle before riding. The throttle should snap back when you release it. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: Compared to a car, a motorcycle needs _____ attention.

options.text: Less
The same amount
More

questions.correctAnswerText: More
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more attention than cars. You must find any problems before riding in traffic or at high speeds.

questions.question: During a crash, wearing a helmet makes a rider:

options.text: Less likely to survive than someone without a helmet.
Just as likely to survive as someone without a helmet.
More likely to survive than someone without a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: More likely to survive than someone without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders wearing helmets. This is true at any speed.

questions.question: What should you know about hearing protection when riding?

options.text: It is not needed if you are wearing a helmet.
It is only recommended for long trips.
It should be used on all rides.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be used on all rides.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet on. Always wear hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Help you blend in with traffic.
Give you an escape route.
Encourage others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you an escape route.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should keep you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Look over their shoulder when the bike turns or curves.
Never hold onto the rider.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over their shoulder when the bike turns or curves.
questions.explanation: Before your passenger gets on, ask them to look over your shoulder in the direction of any turn or curve. This helps you and the bike lean the right way.

questions.question: When cars merge from an entrance ramp, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Assume the merging drivers see them.
Never assume the merging drivers see them.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume the merging drivers see them.
questions.explanation: Give merging cars plenty of space. Do not assume drivers see you. Change lanes away if you can. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed to let them merge safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: This is a warning sign. Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: When someone is passing you, you should:

options.text: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. This is safest. Riding on the left side toward the passing driver is dangerous. Riding on the right side may make the driver return to your lane too quickly.

questions.question: Why is stopping difficult in a turn?

options.text: There is less grip available for stopping when the bike is leaning.
The rider is focused on the turn, not on braking.
The brakes do not work in turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is less grip available for stopping when the bike is leaning.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. When your motorcycle is leaning, some grip is used for the turn. This leaves less grip available for stopping.

questions.question: When the lights on this sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Proceed with caution.
Turn around and find an alternate route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, you must stop completely. Wait until the train has passed and the lights stop flashing before moving. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while stopping, you should:

options.text: Continue to apply the front brake.
Release the front brake and only use the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then apply it firmly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it firmly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks during a quick stop, release the front brake immediately. Then apply it firmly again. Use both front and rear brakes when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: Improper braking:

options.text: Usually has no consequences.
Causes many motorcycle crashes.
Should not be a concern since motorcycles have two brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Causes many motorcycle crashes.
questions.explanation: Improper braking is a major cause of motorcycle crashes. Using correct braking technique is an important part of safe riding.

questions.question: Taking over-the-counter medication before riding:

options.text: Is usually fine because over-the-counter medications are weak.
Is acceptable all the time.
May affect your riding and should be done carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: May affect your riding and should be done carefully.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, can affect your ability to ride safely. Ask your doctor how a new medication might affect your riding or driving.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield can protect you from:

options.text: Noise.
Dust.
Glare.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dust.
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your face if you crash. It also protects you from daily hazards like rocks from other vehicles, wind, dust, dirt, rain, and insects.

questions.question: Smaller vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.

options.text: Closer
Farther away
Larger

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge the speed and distance of small vehicles like motorcycles. Do not assume that drivers of larger vehicles will correctly see your speed and location.

questions.question: Blind spots on motorcycles:

options.text: Are nothing to worry about.
Should be checked regularly by riders.
Don't exist if the motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be checked regularly by riders.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks a normal part of your riding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Signal ahead.
Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold up your body.
Sit at an angle so your arms can support your weight.
Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit upright so your arms can control the motorcycle. Do not sit in a way that requires your arms to hold up your body.

questions.question: Which factor does not play a major role in affecting your blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: Age
The amount of alcohol consumed
Body weight

questions.correctAnswerText: Age
questions.explanation: The main factors that affect BAC are the amount of alcohol consumed, how quickly you drink it, and your body weight. Age does not play a major role.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: If you are being passed, you should:

options.text: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when being passed. This is safest. If you ride on the side near the passing vehicle, you risk a collision. If you ride on the far side, the driver may not return to their lane safely.
